page.layout: One printed page: a single column of running text, with a running head at the top and a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Quis enim pater terrenus naturali amore, impetu impensissimo diligens filium, ipsum sciens & volens permitteret ruere in cruciatus nunquam finiendos, ideoque, quamvis dicendum ò altitudo, nunquid dicendum ò monstrosum? ò voluntas permittens Deo indigna? & natura-li Dei amore effusissimo, quo reprobos salvari obnixè cupit, aliena qui ipsos secundum voluntatem permittentem fineret ruere in exitium æternum, & eo modo vocet, quum aliter vocare possit, salvis omnibus Dei attributis, quo ipsorum damnatio, quam ille naturali amore non vult, longe gravior fit. 2. Non pudet Iesuitam palam agnoscere, voluntatem permittentem esse indignam Dei bonitate, & alienam à voluntate, qua vult naturaliter omnes salvari. Hic contrariæ plane in Deo sint voluntates, oportet, quin imo nunquam videre potui, quomodo Iesuitæ & Arminia-ni contrarietatem inter Dei voluntatem antecedentem, & voluntatem qua maximam humani generis partem permittat peccare, & in æternum perire, diluere possint. 3. Voluntas Dei permittens habet locum tantum in peccatis: atqui incongrue non nullos vocare non est peccatum, sed actus tum justitiæ, tum bonitatis. At vero absurdum est Deum actus justitiæ & bonitatis permissive, non voluntate effectiva facere: nec unquam scriptura bonos actus Dei voluntati permittenti tribuit, nec recta ratio id patitur. Secundum (inquit) voluntatem ordinantem Deus non eligit hunc modum.

page.notes: The text is one continuous paragraph on the scan; the numbers 2. and 3. are inline section numbers, not paragraph breaks. Whether the first line is a fresh paragraph or a continuation from the previous page is not clear from the image, so no cont="true" was set. "Arminia-ni" keeps the printed line-end hyphen; the second half is read as "ni". "Iefuitæ" is read as "Iesuitæ" with long s written as plain s. "permiffiue" is read as "permissive". "modum" is treated as a catchword, being a single word alone at the right below the last line.
